failure_summary.description: Agents selected an associated work or relationship, an etymon, or an adjacent clue answer despite existing rules identifying the requested target.
Agents returned a partial conventional title or entity name, or added an unnecessary given name to an unambiguous surname.
A standalone person-and-office prompt was interpreted as asking for the office rather than the officeholder's jurisdiction.

patch.reasoning: The target-selection and etymology failures are already covered by explicit skill rules, so duplicating them is unwarranted. Clarifying conventional answer forms addresses the repeated partial-title/entity and overlong-person-name mismatches. The standalone officeholder-relation case is isolated here and a similar proposed rule was rejected previously.

edits.target: Use a name form that uniquely identifies the entity: give the complete identifying name when needed, but a surname or shorter form is appropriate when it is unambiguous.
edits.content: Use the context-supported conventional answer form. For a person, use the conventional surname or shorter form when it is unambiguous; include given names only when needed. When a work, organization, or other named entity is requested as a whole, give its complete conventional name or title—not just a familiar prefix or the literal missing token from an embedded blank. Do not add unrelated modifiers.
